title: Chapter 4 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of accessible CSS and visual design.

questions.question: What is the minimum contrast ratio for normal text (less than 24px) to meet WCAG AA?
questions.explanation: WCAG 1.4.3 requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text at Level AA.

questions.question: Large text (24px bold) only needs a contrast ratio of 3:1 to pass AA.
questions.explanation: Large text (≥18.66px bold or ≥24px) has a lower minimum of 3:1.

questions.question: Which CSS property can be used to replace the default focus outline with a custom one?
questions.explanation: You can use outline, border, or box-shadow (commonly combined) to create a visible focus indicator.

questions.question: What is wrong with `button:focus { outline: none; }`?
options: It removes the visual focus indicator, making the button inaccessible to keyboard users
questions.explanation: Removing the outline without a replacement violates WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible.

questions.question: Which media query should you use to adapt your site for users who prefer less animation?
questions.explanation: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is the standard media feature.

questions.question: WCAG 1.4.4 requires that text can be resized up to _____ without loss of content or functionality.
questions.explanation: The Resize Text criterion specifies 200%.

questions.question: What is the maximum flash rate per second allowed to avoid triggering seizures?
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.3.1 prohibits anything that flashes more than 3 times per second.

questions.question: Using colour alone to convey information (e.g., red border for error) is sufficient if the contrast is high enough.
questions.explanation: Colour must not be the only visual means of conveying information; always add text or icons.

questions.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the root font size and thus respects user preferences?
questions.explanation: `rem` is relative to the root element's font size, which users can adjust.

questions.question: What is the recommended maximum line length for readable text?
questions.explanation: 45 to 75 characters per line is the generally accepted comfortable reading length.

questions.question: Which CSS property combination is most performant and accessible for animations?
questions.explanation: `transform` and `opacity` are compositor‑only properties, causing less layout thrashing and being smoother.

questions.question: Forced-colors mode is a Windows feature that overrides your site's colours with a high‑contrast palette. Your site should still be usable in this mode.
questions.explanation: High Contrast Mode (detected via `forced-colors: active`) can strip your custom colours; your layout must still work.

questions.question: What does the `:focus-visible` pseudo-class do?
options: Applies focus styles only when the element is hovered
Applies focus styles based on the user's input modality (keyboard vs mouse)
questions.explanation: `:focus-visible` lets the browser decide when a focus ring is necessary, reducing unnecessary outlines on mouse clicks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `outline-offset`?
options: To change the colour of the outline
To add space between the element's edge and the outline
questions.explanation: `outline-offset` creates a gap, which can make the focus ring more visible and distinct.

questions.question: Why should you avoid justified text alignment for body content?
options: It creates uneven spacing that can be difficult for dyslexic users
questions.explanation: Justified text produces variable word spacing and "rivers of white", disrupting readability.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid WCAG requirement for text spacing?
options: Users must be able to override line height to at least 1.5
Users must be able to change the font family
Users must be able to increase font size to 300%
Users must be able to change background colour
questions.explanation: WCAG 1.4.12 requires that no loss of content occurs when text spacing is overridden to specific minimums.

questions.question: What is the minimum contrast ratio for UI component boundaries (like input borders) as per WCAG 1.4.11?
questions.explanation: UI components and graphical objects must have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours.

questions.question: Using only CSS, you can ensure that a custom element (like a div with onclick) becomes fully accessible.
questions.explanation: CSS alone cannot provide roles, keyboard interaction, or accessible names; ARIA or proper HTML is needed.

questions.question: How can you test if your site works at 200% zoom?
options: Use the browser zoom function and check for horizontal scrolling
questions.explanation: Manually zoom to 200% (Ctrl/Cmd + +) and ensure all content is still usable without horizontal scroll.

questions.question: What does the `prefers-color-scheme` media query allow?
options: Detecting if the user prefers reduced motion
Applying styles for light or dark mode based on OS setting
questions.explanation: `prefers-color-scheme: dark` or `light` allows you to adapt your site to the user's theme preference.
